scope_of_deliverables.value: The Better Cotton Initiative (BCI) is seeking proposals for a Training Cascade Review Survey to evaluate the effectiveness of its training cascade model for delivering capacity strengthening to BCI farmers. The scope, detailed under 'Scope of Work' on page 3, includes: (1) a benchmarking review of existing capacity strengthening models for other ISEAL standards; (2) co-design and execution of an online survey for Programme Partners; and (3) conducting webinars and up to two face-to-face consultations (though Q6 on page 8 clarifies these consultations are now to be conducted remotely). The review will focus on 11 direct BCI countries (Benin, China, Côte d’Ivoire, Egypt, India, Mali, Mozambique, Pakistan, Tajikistan, Türkiye, Uzbekistan) and up to 60 Programme Partners, as confirmed in Q10 (page 9) and Q21 (page 12).
scope_of_deliverables.quote:
Scope of Work
This review will enable BCI, as part of its ISEAL five-year review of capacity strengthening, to decide what to retain, adapt, or redesign in the training cascade model — recognising that the answer may differ by country — and how the Behaviour Change Wheel or similar behaviour change approach should be integrated. For the purposes of this review, the cascade is effective if knowledge reaches farmers with reasonable rigour, is understood by them, and contributes alongside other capability, opportunity and motivation factors to increased practice adoption. We need to avoid the simplistic assumption that the cascade is effective simply because training sessions are delivered.

The review should therefore explore how the training delivered by Partners interacts with other components of behaviour change approaches including the enabling environment (Opportunity) and motivation of farmers as these will also be key determinants of practice adoption. However, the delivery of training on specific topics as evidenced through annually collected Results Indicators currently provides the best proxy data source available to compare with practice adoption outcomes.

BCI will therefore provide the consultant with relevant existing data at kick-off, including anonymised assurance findings and practice adoption indicators, and survey findings should be checked against these. Options for change should be assessed for their expected impact on farmer practice adoption, cost and effort to implement, and feasibility across differing country contexts.

BCI is in the process of updating the training cascades in producer countries that were part of the BCI programme in 2021 and creating new cascades for those countries that have been recently onboarded such as Côte d’Ivoire and Benin. Building on these cascade updates, the expected outputs of this project will be:

• A benchmarking review of existing CS models for other ISEAL standards, particularly those operating in the agricultural sector to highlight best practices being implemented by other standards that could be utilised by BCI, to enhance the effectiveness of BCI’s cascade model – including how other standards use digital tools or AI based approaches to deliver capacity strengthening directly to farmers – and which will inform the options presented in the final report.

• Co-design and run an online survey of Programme Partners (translated as needed) covering: how the cascade operates in practice, where knowledge transfer weakens, actual use of the Behaviour Change Wheel or similar, what digital channels PPs and farmers currently use and PP views on the feasibility of digital delivery direct to farmers in their context, and what PPs would change. The consultant will review BCI’s suggested questions and propose amendments for BCI approval prior to launch. Responses are confidential to the consultant with BCI only receiving anonymised responses.

• Conduct webinars and up to two face-to-face consultations: with Programme Partners, to test and deepen survey findings and explore any discrepancies with existing BCI data; and separately with Country Teams, to gather their perspectives on the PP descriptions

evaluation_criteria.quote:
Evaluation Criteria
Proposals will be evaluated based on the following criteria:
Technical Evaluation Criteria
• Demonstrated understanding of this RFP
• Quality and clarity of the proposed approach and methodology
• Feasibility of the proposed activity plan and timeline, and appropriateness of time allocated to delivering each task
• Relevant professional experience of the proposed consultant(s)
• Quality and relevance of the sample work submitted
Financial Evaluation Criteria
• Quality and clarity of budget provided, and level of detail included
• Alignment of the budget to the activity timeline detailed in the technical proposal
• Value for money
• Adherence to the available budget

vendor_experience_required.value: At least 5 years' experience evaluating or designing farmer training, extension, or training-of-trainers programmes in smallholder and medium farm agriculture. Also required: demonstrated survey design and analysis experience, including working across languages, and experience producing practical recommendations for programme improvement (not academic research alone).
